# VIGIL MEMORY

> A runtime firewall for autonomous AI agents that remembers which agents are
> banned across sessions, devices and process restarts.

An AI agent caught attempting to install the typosquatted package `reqeusts`
is blocked. Kill every process, start a fresh session, and the same agent is
still blocked — because its trust score is a database row rather than history
replayed into a context window.

Recall is a keyed lookup, not a search: **~1ms in-process, ~1-2.6ms over the
local HTTP memory service, ~260ms on the hosted split deployment** where the
memory service runs on a separate host. There are no vectors, no embeddings,
and no LLM call anywhere on the enforcement path.

Memory is the second stage of a six-stage decision pipeline, ahead of the
dependency graph and ahead of any model. A repeat offender is therefore
stopped by one local database read instead of a graph query plus a paid LLM
judgement. Removing the memory layer is a runnable test: the code still
compiles, and the identical blocked call becomes ALLOWED.

## Key facts

- Five memory tiers: HOT session state, WARM agent trust, COLD decision
  journal, REFERENCE runbooks, ARCHIVE retired agents. All five carry live
  data in a single deployment.
- Progressive enforcement ladder: trust 50 → PAUSE at 30 → BLOCK at 10 →
  archived. The ladder survives process restarts; an archived agent stays
  banned because recall falls back to the archive tier.
- Every firewall decision is SHA-256 hash-chained locally and anchored to Base
  Sepolia. The anchored hash equals the local ledger head byte for byte, and
  the contract rejects a tampered claim.
- Backend is SQLite + FTS5 on local disk, PostgreSQL on the hosted
  deployment. The tier schema, enforcement path and archive fallback are
  identical either way.
- Built on a SigNoz fork. Original VIGIL MEMORY code is MIT; the inherited
  fork remains Apache-2.0.

## Common questions

**Does memory survive a restart?** Yes. `demo/memory_demo.sh` kills every
process between sessions and the agent is still blocked, recalled in about a
millisecond, with the denylist deliberately unset so memory is the only thing
that can block.

**What happens if you delete the memory layer?** The build stays green and the
identical call is ALLOWED. That is the point of the deletion test.

**Does it use a vector database?** No. Recall is a primary-key read plus an
FTS5 index. Zero embeddings are computed anywhere.

**Is an LLM involved in blocking an agent?** No. Every block reports
`model=none`. Models are a last resort for genuinely uncertain calls only.

## Limits, stated plainly

- On-chain anchoring is on Base **Sepolia**, not mainnet. Testnet
  transactions carry no economic weight.
- Virtuals ACP job evaluation is live and memory-backed, but on-chain provider
  registration is not complete: the agent's ERC-4337 smart account has no code
  deployed yet, so the status endpoint reports `registered: false`.
- There are no design partners. None are claimed.
